Delta Air Lines Flight 191 (August 2, 1985, Dallas/Fort Worth)

The Lockheed L-1011 was on approach when it flew into a microburst under a thunderstorm. All three cockpit crew members were male: Captain Edward “Ted” Connors (pilot monitoring), First Officer Rudolph “Rudy” Price (pilot flying), and Flight Engineer Nicholas Nassick. Price explicitly noted lightning “right ahead of us.” The crew continued the approach anyway. The NTSB determined the probable causes included the flight crew’s decision to initiate and continue the approach into a cumulonimbus cloud they observed containing visible lightning, combined with inadequate procedures/training for avoiding or escaping low-altitude wind shear and the lack of real-time hazard information at the time

Microbursts were still poorly understood in the mid-1980s (Fujita’s research was relatively recent, and detection systems were limited), so many crews of the period continued into weather that later training and technology would flag as no-go. The FO was actively flying and part of the joint decision process; the accident was not framed as one pilot overriding the other. Similar dynamics appear in other period cases such as USAir Flight 1016 (1994, Charlotte), where an all-male crew also continued into microburst conditions and then had coordination problems during the escape attempt.
